title: Business Financial Analyst
description:
At GAF, we cover more than buildings. We cover each other. No matter what role, tenure, or track, under this roof you are empowered to be there for your teammates, your customers, and especially your community. Under this roof, we don’t back down from hard work– we support one another in pursuit of something bigger. We define the future while leading the present. And under this roof, we own our opportunities. Becoming the market leader only happens when everyone feels they have the opportunity, and the support, to thrive. We are GAF. And under this roof, we protect what matters most.

**Job Summary**  
The Financial Analyst serves as a strategic partner to functional leadership, providing critical oversight of corporate cost structures through tracking and reporting of spend. Utilizing core financial and analytical skills, the Financial Analyst will develop a comprehensive understanding of each function's cost structure and will partner with functional leadership to drive overall spend efficiency as well as adherence to spending targets and budgets. This role will also have various responsibilities related to forecasting and the annual budgeting process, ensuring the delivery of projected spend within plan timelines. As part of a broader team focused on SG&A spending, the Financial Analyst will be a critical part of the monthly close process providing insight into spending vs. performance targets and highlighting variances that require review or adjustments by the corporate accounting team.  
  
  
  
  
**Essential Duties**

* Support the monthly expense review process for corporate functions, collaborating with department heads to analyze actual vs budget variances.

  

* Analyze spend details to identify opportunities for savings.

  

* Work on process efficiency and improvement of the monthly close activities.

  

* Review and analysis of ad-hoc financial reporting and special analytical projects as assigned.

  

* Drive reporting utilizing SAC, developing reporting views that drive accountability for business partners.

  

* Lead role in the Annual Budget process – developing analysis, preparing budget estimates, and finalizing budgets for leadership approval.

  

* Support monthly forecasting efforts, allowing the FP&A team to have a better view of the most up-to-date trends in spend by function.

  

* Review expense items and partner with accounting for items that need to be accrued or re-classed to proper accounts.

  

* Conduct these activities while ensuring that internal and external standards are being met.

  

* Support the launch of SAP OPEX as part of Project Skyline through testing and user training.

  

* Partner with workforce planning team to understand headcount moves, additions, and terminations, ensuring that spend projections reflect changes as needed.

**Qualifications Required**

* Bachelor’s Degree accounting, finance or related degree required
* 3+ years of experience required.
* Excellent computer skills/Proficient in Microsoft Excel

**Qualifications Preferred**

* Ability to manage competing priorities under tight timelines.
* Strong analytical & problem solving skills.
* Developing the ability to influence and gain buy-in when needed.
* Good general business knowledge.
* Ability to build relationships across different levels of the organization.
* Excellent working knowledge of Google suite, particularly Google Sheets and Slides.
Good knowledge of GAF Systems, Applications, & Technologies.

title: FP&A Analyst III
description:
Overview:

We are seeking a highly analytical and detail-oriented FP&A Analyst III to support expense analysis, planning, forecasting, and reporting. This individual-contributor role is designed for an experienced finance professional who can independently manage recurring analytical deliverables, work effectively with large datasets, and translate financial results into clear business insights.

The role will partner closely with business stakeholders and finance teams to support expense management, budgeting, allocations, and management reporting. The successful candidate will combine strong financial acumen, technical capability, and a hands-on approach, while identifying opportunities to improve processes and automate recurring FP&A workflows.

The ideal candidate demonstrates strong ownership, accuracy, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to leverage financial systems, data tools, and emerging technologies, including AI, to improve efficiency and insight generation. **This role will require on-site attendance 4 days per week****in Jersey City, NJ.**

Responsibilities:

* Analyze expenses across business units and functions, including actual versus budget, forecast, and prior-period variance analysis; identify and clearly explain key drivers.
* Support annual budgeting, periodic forecasting, and long-range planning activities for expenses, including the development and maintenance of allocation methodologies and cost drivers.
* Prepare recurring expense reporting packages, management analyses, and clear presentations for finance and business stakeholders.
* Maintain and enhance financial models, datasets, reports, and dashboards using Excel, Power Query, Power BI, and related tools.
* Work with large, structured datasets; perform reconciliations and validation procedures to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency across planning and reporting outputs.
* Support the design, testing, and implementation of expense planning and reporting processes within Oracle or similar enterprise financial systems.
* Partner with business and functional teams to understand expense trends, operating drivers, risks, and opportunities.
* Identify and implement practical improvements to recurring expense reporting, forecasting, and data-preparation processes.
* Use automation and AI-enabled tools where appropriate to enhance financial analysis, reporting quality, and workflow efficiency.
* Maintain clear documentation, controls, assumptions, and audit trails for financial models, allocation processes, and reporting outputs.
* Independently manage assigned deliverables, escalate issues promptly, and meet established reporting and planning deadlines.
* Support ad hoc financial analysis and special projects as needed.

Qualifications:

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field.
* Typically 4-7 years of relevant experience in FP&A, expense reporting, financial analysis, accounting, or a related corporate finance role.
* Solid understanding of financial statements, budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, cost allocations, and expense management concepts.
* Experience in the insurance or broader financial services industry is preferred; strong familiarity with insurance concepts is a plus.
* Advanced Excel skills, including experience building and maintaining financial models and working with large datasets.
* Proficiency with Power Query and/or Power BI is preferred.
* Experience with enterprise financial systems such as Oracle, SAP, Hyperion, or FCCS is preferred.
* Demonstrated experience improving reporting processes, automating recurring workflows, or increasing data quality and efficiency.
* Exposure to data analytics, automation, or AI-enabled solutions in a finance context is preferred.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain financial concepts and analytical findings clearly to finance and non-finance stakeholders.
* Big Four or similar professional-services experience is a plus.

**Key Competencies**

* Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
* Ability to work independently, take ownership of assigned deliverables, and follow through to completion.
* Hands-on approach with the ability to work in the details while understanding the broader business context.
* Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to prioritize multiple deliverables and perform effectively in a fast-paced environment.
* Proactive communication and effective cross-functional partnership.
* Intellectual curiosity, adaptability, and willingness to learn new systems and tools.
* Continuous-improvement mindset focused on automation, efficiency, controls, and scalable processes.
* Comfort working with evolving processes, complex financial data, and changing business requirements.

**Role Scope**

This is an individual-contributor position with no direct reports or people-management responsibilities. The FP&A Analyst III is expected to independently execute assigned analyses and recurring processes, collaborate across functions, and provide reliable, decision-useful financial information to stakeholders.

What We Offer:

AmTrust Financial Services offers a competitive compensation package and excellent career advancement opportunities. Our benefits include Medical & Dental Plans, Life Insurance, including eligible spouses & children, Health Care Flexible Spending, Dependent Care, 401k Savings Plans, Paid Time Off.

AmTrust strives to create a diverse and inclusive culture where thoughts and ideas of all employees are appreciated and respected. This concept encompasses but is not limited to human differences with regard to race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, culture, religion or disabilities.

AmTrust values excellence and recognizes that by embracing the diverse backgrounds, skills, and perspectives of its workforce, it will sustain a competitive advantage and remain an employer of choice. title: Senior Financial Analyst - Marketing Finance
description:
**About the Role**

We are seeking an experienced finance professional to support Bloomberg's Marketing organization, with a primary focus on Advertising & Marketing (A&M) expense management and financial planning.

  

This role will serve as a key finance partner to Marketing managers, supporting project budgeting, forecasting, and financial outlooks while providing insight into spend, trends, risks, and opportunities. The role will also have hands-on responsibility for the monthly close process and ensuring the accuracy and integrity of Marketing financial results.

  

The ideal candidate combines strong FP&A experience and financial acumen with attention to detail, an ownership mindset, and strong relationship-building skills. This individual should be equally comfortable managing the details of financial processes and partnering with the business to understand priorities, challenge assumptions, and provide thoughtful financial guidance.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

• Partner closely with Marketing managers to develop project budgets, forecasts, and financial outlooks across Advertising & Marketing spend.

• Manage A&M budgeting and forecasting, developing a strong understanding of Marketing initiatives, spending plans, commitments, and key financial drivers.

• Own the monthly close process for A&M expenses, including accruals, reclasses, and other adjustments necessary to ensure accurate financial reporting.

• Analyze actual spend against budget and forecast, identifying and communicating key variances, trends, risks, and opportunities.

• Support periodic forecasts and the annual operating plan (AOP), working with Marketing stakeholders to develop assumptions and maintain an informed view of the expense outlook.

• Maintain and manage Marketing cost center structures and hierarchies to support accurate financial reporting, planning, and controls.

• Develop clear, executive-ready reporting and analysis that provides visibility into Marketing spend, financial performance, and key takeaways.

• Partner across Marketing, Finance, Accounting, and other cross-functional teams to resolve financial issues and ensure appropriate accounting and reporting of Marketing expenses.

• Develop and maintain financial models and analyses to support resource allocation, project evaluation, and other business decisions.

• Proactively identify opportunities to improve and automate financial reporting, forecasting, close, and planning processes.

• Develop and evolve ROI analysis across Marketing channels, in partnership with Marketing stakeholders, to assess the effectiveness and impact of investments, helping drive future resource allocation decisions.

  

**Qualifications & Experience**

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.

• Minimum 5 years of relevant finance experience, with demonstrated hands-on experience in FP&A, expense management, budgeting, forecasting, or financial reporting.

• Strong understanding of financial planning and monthly close processes, including accruals, reclasses, variance analysis, and expense recognition.

• Demonstrated experience partnering directly with business stakeholders to develop budgets, understand spending plans, and manage financial outlooks.

• Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to analyze financial data, identify key drivers, and develop actionable insights.

• Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and deliver high-quality work within recurring financial deadlines.

• High attention to detail with a strong sense of ownership, accountability, and follow-through.

• Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively across Finance and non-Finance stakeholders.

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, with experience using enterprise financial systems such as SAP, Oracle, EPM, or similar platforms.

  

**Key Attributes**

• Hands-on finance professional with a strong ownership and execution mindset.

• Collaborative business partner who builds effective relationships and credibility with stakeholders.

• Financially disciplined and detail-oriented, with the ability to connect detailed financial activity to broader business priorities.

• Comfortable challenging assumptions, asking thoughtful questions, and bringing an independent financial perspective.

• Proactive and solutions-oriented, with the ability to identify issues and drive them through resolution.

• Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment and balancing recurring financial responsibilities with evolving business needs.

• Process-minded, with an interest in leveraging systems, data, and automation to improve financial management.

title: Senior Financial Analyst FP&A – Lifestyle Brands
description:
Overview:

**Catalyst Brands** is seeking a **Senior Financial Analyst** to support financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and business analysis for our **Lifestyle Brands** division, namely Aéropostale, Lucky Brand, and Nautica. This hybrid role is based in our **New York, NY** corporate office or our **Lyndhurst, NJ** finance office (preferred).

This position partners directly with Finance, Accounting, and Brand business leaders to evaluate performance across retail, e-commerce, and wholesale channels. You will analyze business drivers, explain financial variances, and deliver actionable insights that shape strategic business decisions.

The ideal candidate is an independent, self-starting professional who can own their work from end-to-end. You should blend proficient financial planning and analysis (FP&A) skills with a corporate accounting foundation, possessing an innate curiosity, a meticulous process for validating data, and the ability to translate operational activities into clear, strategic financial narratives.

Responsibilities:

* **Financial Planning & Analysis:** Drive and support annual budgeting, monthly forecasting, and long-range planning across retail, e-commerce, wholesale, and corporate operations. We are looking for hands-on partners who actively build and shape forecasts, not just compile reports.
* **Independent Ownership:** Take personal ownership of assigned business areas, forecasts, or recurring deliverables with limited supervision.
* **Analytical Modeling:** Build, maintain, and substantially improve sophisticated, driver-based financial models in Excel with clearly documented, reasonable assumptions that help the business make decisions.
* **Variance & Performance Analysis:** Analyze sales, gross margin, operating expenses (SG&A), and overall profitability against budget, forecast, and prior periods. Proactively investigate unexpected variances, identify underlying root causes, and recommend actionable solutions.
* **Accounting & General Ledger Integrity:** Analyze GL accounts and transaction-level details to validate monthly financial results and explain how accounting activity flows into financial statements. Partner closely with Accounting during month-end close to assess accrual needs and resolve discrepancies.
* **Commercial Analysis:** Partner cross-functionally with non-finance teams to understand operating plans and analyze the impacts of pricing strategies, product volume, category mix, and product costs on sales and gross margin performance across different brand channels.
* **Executive Presentation & Communication:** Partner cross-functionally to prepare and present clear financial results, forecasts, and strategic recommendations. You must be able to explain complex financial concepts clearly and confidently to both Finance and non-Finance business partners.

Qualifications:

**Required:**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related quantitative field.
* **Experience:** 2 or more years of relevant, hands-on experience in FP&A, corporate finance, or a combination of corporate accounting and financial analysis.
* **Advanced Excel Capabilities:** High proficiency with advanced Excel features (including lookups, SUMIFS, index/match, pivot tables, and driver-based modeling) with a demonstrated ability to troubleshoot formulas.
* **Data Validation & Accuracy:** A structured, rigorous process for self-auditing, reconciling, and checking your own work for accuracy and completeness before presenting results to leadership.
* **Communication & Collaboration:** Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; a proven ability to work productively with non-finance partners to resolve issues and improve forecast accuracy.

**Preferred:**

* **Business Model Knowledge:** Solid working knowledge of retail (brick-and-mortar/e-commerce) and/or wholesale business models, including their unique financial drivers.
* **Industry Experience:** Prior finance or accounting experience within the apparel, footwear, retail, or consumer packaged goods (CPG) sectors.
* **Enterprise Systems:** Experience with enterprise systems and reporting tools, such as Oracle, OneStream, or MicroStrategy.

**What You Get**

If eligible, we offer a competitive benefits package including medical/dental/vision, term life insurance, paid vacation/holidays\*, and 401(k) with Company match. All associates are eligible for an associate discount on Catalyst Brands merchandise. For paid holidays, associates who are eligible for paid vacation (MTO) are also eligible for eight paid holidays during the calendar year. All store hourly associates scheduled to work on a designated holiday will receive additional compensation. \*For paid vacation days, as well as eligibility requirements for other benefits, please visit www.catalystbrandsbenefits.com

**About Catalyst**

Catalyst Brands reflects the bringing together the rich heritages of our brands with modern excitement and a new vision for success. Five iconic brands came together under a unified powerhouse portfolio to celebrate the essence of American style. We will leverage our rich history, resources and best-in-class industry talent to further build the success of our brands. At Catalyst we are united in one shared purpose: We exist to ignite America’s most beloved retail brands to make fashion accessible to all.

Working at Catalyst means joining a dedicated team of associates who are encouraged to be uniquely themselves in a safe, caring and welcoming environment. It is a place where careers prosper, accomplishments are celebrated and diversity flourishes. It’s a place that’s meant for you.

For more opportunities to join our team please visit our careers page.

title: FP&A Analyst - Car Rental Business
description:

At Avis Budget Group, we’re driven to be the best vehicle rental company in the world, together. * Employee discounts, including discounted prices on the purchase of Avis/Budget cars
* Access to an Employee Assistance Program for services including counseling, financial and legal consultation, referrals for care service and more

* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills — comfortable digging into data to find the "why"
* Working knowledge of P&L structure and financial analysis fundamentals
* Clear written and verbal communication skills; able to work cross-functionally
* Proficiency in Microsoft Excel; comfort with the broader Microsoft Office suite
* SQL/Python proficiency a strong plus
* Familiarity with applying AI/automation tools to reporting and analysis workflows is a plus
* A genuine curiosity and enthusiasm for the business, not just the numbers
* Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, or related field (or equivalent experience)

title: Senior Financial Analyst FP&A – Lifestyle Brands
description:
Overview:

**Catalyst Brands** is seeking a **Senior Financial Analyst** to support financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and business analysis for our **Lifestyle Brands** division, namely Aéropostale, Lucky Brand, and Nautica. This hybrid role is based in our **Lyndhurst, New Jersey** corporate office (preferred).

This position partners directly with Finance, Accounting, and Brand business leaders to evaluate performance across retail, e-commerce, and wholesale channels. You will analyze business drivers, explain financial variances, and deliver actionable insights that shape strategic business decisions.

The ideal candidate is an independent, self-starting professional who can own their work from end-to-end. You should blend proficient financial planning and analysis (FP&A) skills with a corporate accounting foundation, possessing an innate curiosity, a meticulous process for validating data, and the ability to translate operational activities into clear, strategic financial narratives.

Responsibilities:

* **Financial Planning & Analysis:** Drive and support annual budgeting, monthly forecasting, and long-range planning across retail, e-commerce, wholesale, and corporate operations. We are looking for hands-on partners who actively build and shape forecasts, not just compile reports.
* **Independent Ownership:** Take personal ownership of assigned business areas, forecasts, or recurring deliverables with limited supervision.
* **Analytical Modeling:** Build, maintain, and substantially improve sophisticated, driver-based financial models in Excel with clearly documented, reasonable assumptions that help the business make decisions.
* **Variance & Performance Analysis:** Analyze sales, gross margin, operating expenses (SG&A), and overall profitability against budget, forecast, and prior periods. Proactively investigate unexpected variances, identify underlying root causes, and recommend actionable solutions.
* **Accounting & General Ledger Integrity:** Analyze GL accounts and transaction-level details to validate monthly financial results and explain how accounting activity flows into financial statements. Partner closely with Accounting during month-end close to assess accrual needs and resolve discrepancies.
* **Commercial Analysis:** Partner cross-functionally with non-finance teams to understand operating plans and analyze the impacts of pricing strategies, product volume, category mix, and product costs on sales and gross margin performance across different brand channels.
* **Executive Presentation & Communication:** Partner cross-functionally to prepare and present clear financial results, forecasts, and strategic recommendations. You must be able to explain complex financial concepts clearly and confidently to both Finance and non-Finance business partners.

Qualifications:

**Required:**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related quantitative field.
* **Experience:** 2 or more years of relevant, hands-on experience in FP&A, corporate finance, or a combination of corporate accounting and financial analysis.
* **Advanced Excel Capabilities:** High proficiency with advanced Excel features (including lookups, SUMIFS, index/match, pivot tables, and driver-based modeling) with a demonstrated ability to troubleshoot formulas.
* **Data Validation & Accuracy:** A structured, rigorous process for self-auditing, reconciling, and checking your own work for accuracy and completeness before presenting results to leadership.
* **Communication & Collaboration:** Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; a proven ability to work productively with non-finance partners to resolve issues and improve forecast accuracy.

**Preferred:**

* **Business Model Knowledge:** Solid working knowledge of retail (brick-and-mortar/e-commerce) and/or wholesale business models, including their unique financial drivers.
* **Industry Experience:** Prior finance or accounting experience within the apparel, footwear, retail, or consumer packaged goods (CPG) sectors.
* **Enterprise Systems:** Experience with enterprise systems and reporting tools, such as **Oracle, OneStream, or MicroStrategy**.

**What You Get**

If eligible, we offer a competitive benefits package including medical/dental/vision, term life insurance, paid vacation/holidays\*, and 401(k) with Company match. All associates are eligible for an associate discount on Catalyst Brands merchandise. For paid holidays, associates who are eligible for paid vacation (MTO) are also eligible for eight paid holidays during the calendar year. All store hourly associates scheduled to work on a designated holiday will receive additional compensation. \*For paid vacation days, as well as eligibility requirements for other benefits, please visit www.catalystbrandsbenefits.com

**About Catalyst**

Catalyst Brands reflects the bringing together the rich heritages of our brands with modern excitement and a new vision for success. Five iconic brands came together under a unified powerhouse portfolio to celebrate the essence of American style. We will leverage our rich history, resources and best-in-class industry talent to further build the success of our brands. At Catalyst we are united in one shared purpose: We exist to ignite America’s most beloved retail brands to make fashion accessible to all.

Working at Catalyst means joining a dedicated team of associates who are encouraged to be uniquely themselves in a safe, caring and welcoming environment. It is a place where careers prosper, accomplishments are celebrated and diversity flourishes. It’s a place that’s meant for you.

For more opportunities to join our team please visit our careers page.

title: Senior Claims Manager - Quality & Compliance
description:
**About the Role**  
  
Uber is home to one of the largest and most unique claims programs in the world. As our Sr. Claims Manager, Quality & Compliance, you will set the strategy and lead the operating model for claims quality and compliance, spanning First Notice of Loss (FNOL) quality assurance, the Claims Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) control environment, audit readiness, and quality and compliance oversight of external claims partners.  
  
You will translate business priorities into a coordinated roadmap with clear ownership, appropriate resourcing, and measurable outcomes. Working with Claims leadership, Operations, Financial Risk Management, Accounting, auditors, and carrier partners, you will build the systems and governance that improve quality, strengthen controls, and address recurring issues at their source.  
  
This role requires a seasoned people leader who combines deep claims expertise with sound business judgment and the ability to lead through ambiguity. You will build and develop a well-rounded team, balance autonomy with coaching, and serve as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders. Your work will shape how internal teams and external partners deliver consistent, compliant claims experiences and prepare for future business needs.  
  
**What You’ll Do**  

* Set strategy and priorities. Define and lead the claims quality and compliance roadmap, connecting FNOL quality, control effectiveness, audit readiness, and partner performance to broader Claims and company priorities. Make clear tradeoffs across initiatives and align resources to the highest-impact needs.
* Build and develop the team. Lead a team of claims quality and compliance professionals, define accountabilities, and develop the capabilities needed to deliver the roadmap. Provide thoughtful coaching, delegate with clear expectations, and create a collaborative environment that supports learning, candid feedback, and sustainable performance.
* Design systems that deliver consistent results. Establish governance, decision rights, performance measures, and structured business reviews that align internal teams and external partners around shared objectives. Adjust priorities and capacity as risks, business needs, and performance change.
* Lead the FNOL quality framework. Direct the design and continuous improvement of QA methodologies, sampling approaches, scorecards, calibration, and root-cause analysis. Translate findings into improvements in processes, training, and tooling, and verify that corrective actions produce sustained results.
* Lead Claims SOX control governance. Oversee control matrices, narratives, evidence readiness, and remediation across the Claims control environment. Coordinate control design and testing with control owners, Financial Risk Management, Accounting, and auditors; establish clear accountability for timely deficiency resolution.
* Lead audit engagement for Claims. Serve as the senior Claims point of contact for SOX, statutory, and carrier audits. Clearly explain processes, risks, control design, and operating effectiveness, and coordinate accurate, timely responses to audit requests and findings.
* Strengthen external partner accountability. Partner with carrier and third-party administrator stakeholders and internal Claims leaders to establish consistent quality and compliance expectations, review performance, and drive corrective action on systemic issues.
* Drive cross-functional change. Lead complex improvements across operational workflows, tooling, and training. Bring structure to ambiguous problems, align stakeholders on requirements and tradeoffs, and guide initiatives from problem definition through implementation, adoption, and measurement.

* Minimum 7 years of professional experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**  

* 10+ years of professional experience.
* 5+ years of people management experience
* 3+ years of experience dedicated to audit, SOX, or regulatory compliance.
* Prior experience as a property and casualty (P&C) claims adjuster or within a gig-economy claims team.
* AIC, SCLA, or CPCU designation.
* Auto insurance claims handling or management experience.
* Prior Big Four or large public-company SOX audit exposure.
* Experience managing third-party administrators or carrier partners.
* Demonstrated ability to define a strategy and translate it into an actionable roadmap across multiple complex workstreams, including priorities, ownership, resourcing, and measurable outcomes.

title: FP&A Manager
description:
Vendelux is building the category-defining platform for event marketing intelligence.

Events are one of the largest and most impactful marketing channels, yet historically one of the least measurable. Vendelux brings transparency and performance to this space — helping companies discover, evaluate, and optimize their event strategy with data.

Our platform powers thousands of event decisions by delivering proprietary, AI-driven insights across hundreds of thousands of events globally. At the core of our platform is a robust ecosystem of event organizer partnerships — where organizers share first-party data, enabling richer insights for customers while receiving benchmarking and audience intelligence in return. From identifying the highest ROI conferences to enabling targeted meeting programs, Vendelux helps companies turn events into a predictable and scalable growth engine.

In addition, Vendelux Meetings extends our platform by turning insights into pipeline — using AI to identify high-value attendees and proactively book 1:1 meetings between our customers and their ideal prospects at events. This enables go-to-market teams to drive measurable ROI and maximize every event interaction.

Founded in 2021, Vendelux is a Series B SaaS company backed by top-tier investors including FirstMark. We partner with many of the fastest-growing companies in the world, and our team includes leaders from Bain, ZoomInfo, Shutterstock, FanDuel, Compass, Airbnb, Forter and beyond.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

Vendelux is looking for an FP&A Manager to own our financial model and the reporting behind our growth story. You'll take detailed accounting output and turn it into forecasts, hiring-plan-driven scenarios and board-ready materials, bringing together data from across our SaaS tech stack. You'll work closely with our COO and executive team. Success looks like a financial model leadership trusts, board and investor materials that tell a clear story, and fundraising materials that are ready when we need them.

This role is based in our NYC office.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* Own Vendelux's financial model end to end, from accounting actuals through the forecast.
* Build multiple forecast scenarios grounded in detailed hiring plans.
* Turn detailed accounting output from our accounting team into forecasts and plans.
* Lead the financial preparation for fundraising, including the data room and the financial story behind it.
* Prepare board decks and investor presentations that clearly communicate performance and outlook.
* Report on the SaaS metrics that matter most to leadership, the board and investors.
* Pull pipeline and revenue data from HubSpot for board and leadership reporting.
* Bring together data from disparate systems, including Maxio, HubSpot and QuickBooks Online, into a single, reliable view of the business.
* Work hands-on with revenue operations data to connect pipeline and bookings to the forecast.
* Continuously improve how the model and reporting are structured so they scale with the business.

**WHO YOU ARE**

* 5+ years of experience in FP&A or strategic finance.
* Experience in FP&A at a venture-backed SaaS company that has scaled through Series B or C.
* Deep expertise in SaaS business models and financial metrics.
* Advanced financial modeling skills, with a track record of owning and building a company's operating model.
* Hands-on experience preparing board decks, investor presentations and financial reporting.
* Experience with a SaaS finance and GTM tech stack similar to ours, such as Maxio, HubSpot and QuickBooks Online.
* Strong skills pulling and reconciling data from multiple systems, including pipeline data from a CRM.
* A builder who takes pride in designing a financial model that's elegant, flexible and easy for others to use.
* Equally comfortable in the accounting detail and in the story the numbers tell.
* Curious about revenue operations data and eager to go beyond traditional FP&A to get the full picture.
* Clear, concise communicator who turns complex analysis into insight for executives and the board.
* Energized by high-visibility work like board reporting and fundraising.
* Intellectually curious, with a strong sense of ownership.
* Genuinely excited about Vendelux and what we're building.
* Background in venture capital, private equity or investment banking
* Experience supporting a company through a fundraise or investor diligence process
* Hands-on experience with Maxio, HubSpot or QuickBooks Online specifically

**BENEFITS**

* Competitive base salary and bonus
* Equity
* Healthcare covering medical, dental and vision
* 401(k)
* Catered lunch every day in our NYC office
* Unlimited PTO plus two company-wide shutdowns during the July 4th week and the Christmas – New Year's week

The Director maintains comprehensive oversight of assigned credits, including financial performance and trend analysis, covenant compliance, reporting requirements, risk ratings, and emerging risks.

* Maintain comprehensive oversight of an assigned portfolio of commercial loans and proactively identify emerging risks.
* Complete credit reviews, risk-rating assessments, and ongoing portfolio monitoring, and present portfolio updates and risk assessments to senior management and credit committees.
* Manage portfolio administration, including financial-performance monitoring, covenant compliance, exception reporting, facility renewals and amendments, and coordination and management of the bank group.
* Monitor sponsor activity, industry dynamics, and macroeconomic developments impacting portfolio companies. Identify emerging risks and develop mitigation strategies.
* Review and negotiate credit documentation in consultation with legal counsel.
* Develop and maintain relationships with private equity sponsors, management teams, investment bankers, and lending partners to support portfolio oversight and identify future business opportunities.
* Review and analyze borrower operating performance, liquidity, leverage trends, covenant compliance, and cash flow generation.
* Evaluate amendment, waiver, acquisition, add-on investment, and refinancing requests.

* Lead portfolio management activities for criticized and challenged credits, including development of risk-mitigation strategies, amendment and restructuring negotiations, liquidity monitoring, and coordination with internal workout and risk teams.

Evaluate transaction risks and recommend appropriate covenant, collateral, pricing, and structural protections. Prepare and present underwriting recommendations to credit committees and senior management. Support syndication and lender presentation activities. Assist with training and / or mentoring of Analyst / Associate team members.

* 7+ years of relevant leveraged finance, underwriting, or portfolio management experience.
* Demonstrated experience managing middle-market leveraged loan portfolios.
* Experience managing borrower amendments, waivers, restructurings, and refinancing activities.
* Experience in banking, commercial lending, private credit, underwriting, financial analysis, credit analysis, auditing, or collateral management.
* Experience with borrower and sponsor relationship management.
* Completion of a formal credit training program preferred.
* Advanced understanding of leveraged lending structures, cash flow underwriting, enterprise valuation methodologies, debt capacity analysis, covenant structures, sponsor equity dynamics, and leveraged buyout transaction modeling.
* Demonstrated experience underwriting and/or managing private equity sponsor-backed middle-market companies.
* Experience presenting credit recommendations, portfolio reviews, and risk assessments to senior management and credit approval committees.
* Excellent communication (verbal and written), interpersonal and organizational skills.
* Highly analytical and detail-oriented, with strong problem-solving capabilities.
* Ability to work independently with demonstrated strong time management skills.
* Well-developed presentation and relationship-building skills.
* High level of accountability and the ability to effectively prioritize tasks.
* Technical: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, including financial forecasting and modeling.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Company**
-----------

Federal Reserve Bank of New YorkWhen you work at the New York Fed, you have the opportunity to make an impact in our communities and across the nation. Our mission-driven, curious, and dedicated colleagues apply their diverse perspectives and unique talents to support the strength of the U.S. economy and stability of the global financial system. At the Bank, we work full-time onsite with our teams. We believe being physically together allows us to draw on our collective strengths, while recognizing that the ability to work flexibly from time to time remains important to achieving our mission.

**Our Unique Work:**

The FRBNY is exposed to credit risk through its provision of financial services to second district depository institutions and execution of market operations at the direction of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), as fiscal agent of the United States and for various official accountholders. More specifically, counterparty credit exposures arise from Discount Window lending, intraday extensions of credit through counterparties’ use of FRBNY payment systems and services, open market trading activities, Federal Reserve lending facilities and liquidity programs, and other activities. Trading activities include outright securities transactions, securities repurchase (repo) and reverse repo agreements, foreign exchange transactions, and foreign exchange swaps.

The Counterparty Credit Risk (CCR) team of the Markets Group is responsible for monitoring and assessing the credit risk of a diverse group of counterparties, identifying institutions that pose a heightened level of risk to the Bank, measuring the magnitude of such risk and implementing risk controls. CCR also participates in internal discussions concerning the trade-offs between policy benefits and risk exposure from extending credit and other topical financial issues.

**How You’ll Make an Impact as a Credit Risk Specialist:**

* Perform credit analyses of various types of depository institutions with FRBNY accounts and/or services, maintain internal risk ratings, and implement credit risk mitigation measures in accordance with Federal Reserve System (FRS) and FRBNY policies. Provide input into intraday credit decisions.

**Fitch Ratings is currently seeking Associate Analysts based out of our New York office.**

  

Fitch Ratings is a leading provider of credit ratings, commentary, and research. **Role Summary:** Fanatics Collectibles is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Manager to join the Royalty Accounting team, reporting directly to the Director of Royalty Accounting team. * Partner with IT, Data & Analytics, and Finance Systems teams to improve royalty system integrations, automation, and reporting capabilities.
* Support process mapping, workflow optimization, and testing for new royalty reporting tools and system enhancements.
* Collaborate with Legal, Licensing, FP&A, IT, Operations, and external licensors to address audit inquiries and operational risks.

* Direct experience supporting external royalty audits and licensing compliance reviews.

**Position Summary and Role Impact:**  
The VP, Controller, Head of Financial Reporting and Consolidation, is responsible for overseeing the company’s financial reporting, financial consolidation, technical accounting, equity and compensation accounting. This role ensures the integrity, accuracy, and timeliness of financial statements and external disclosures in accordance with U.S. GAAP and applicable requirements.

The position oversees monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting, including financial consolidation, equity-based compensation, payroll and benefits accounting and external audits. The role also maintains effective accounting policies, internal controls and financial reporting systems. Working closely with Accounting, FP&A, HR, Legal, SOX, Internal Audit, and external auditors, this individual will strengthen financial reporting controls, drive operational excellence and continuously improve the company’s accounting and reporting processes.

**Essential Functions:**

**SEC and External Financial Reporting**

* Lead the preparation, review, and timely delivery of monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements and external deliverables.
* Oversee U.S. GAAP financial statements, footnotes, and supporting financial disclosures, including SEC filings where applicable.
* Manage quarterly external reviews and annual financial statement audits, coordinating deliverables and resolving audit matters.
* Ensure the accuracy, completeness and consistency of financial statements and external financial communications.
* Manage reporting calendars, disclosure checklists, filing documentation, and cross-functional review processes.
* Coordinate with Legal, external auditors, and internal stakeholders on financial reporting requirements and disclosures.

**Financial Consolidation and Corporate Accounting**

* Oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual financial consolidation processes, including intercompany eliminations and consolidated financial statement preparation.
* Ensure accurate recording of transactions and consolidation adjustments in accordance with U.S. GAAP.
* Review account reconciliations, journal entries, and supporting schedules for significant and complex accounting areas.
* Establish and maintain effective financial close and consolidation procedures.
* Drive improvements in close/ consolidation timelines, reporting accuracy and process scalability.

**Payroll, Benefits, and Incentive Compensation Accounting**

* Oversee accounting and financial reporting for payroll, employee benefits, bonuses and other incentive compensation programs.
* Ensure appropriate recognition, accrual, classification, and disclosure of compensation-related expenses and liabilities under U.S. GAAP.
* Maintain effective controls over compensation accounting, including completeness and accuracy of related financial information.

**Equity and Equity Compensation Accounting, Reporting, and Administration**

* Oversee accounting and disclosure for equity-based compensation programs and ensure compliance with applicable U.S. GAAP requirements, including ASC 718.
* Manage equity compensation expense calculations, valuation inputs, expense recognition, and related reconciliations.
* Oversee equity award activity, vesting schedules, forfeitures, modifications, settlements, and related accounting records.
* Partner with HR, Legal, stock plan administrators, and external service providers on equity plan administration and reporting.
* Oversee shareholder’s equity accounting, roll forwards, transactions and related financial statement disclosures.

**Technical Accounting and Accounting Policy**

* Develop, maintain, and communicate accounting policies, procedures, and technical accounting guidance.
* Prepare and review technical accounting memo for significant transactions, complex estimates, and accounting judgments under U.S. GAAP.
* Monitor new accounting standards and regulatory developments and assess their impact on the company.
* Coordinate with external auditors on significant accounting conclusions and disclosure matters.

**Financial Reporting Systems Management**

* Oversee the administration, maintenance, and continuous improvement of financial reporting and consolidation systems, including Oracle, Workiva, FCCS, and Smart View.
* Manage system configurations, reporting structures, consolidation rules, chart-of-accounts mappings, and financial reporting workflows, as applicable.
* Ensure the integrity, accuracy, and consistency of financial data across source systems, consolidation platforms, and external reporting tools.
* Lead system enhancements, upgrades, automation initiatives, and process improvements to strengthen reporting efficiency and accuracy.
* Establish appropriate access controls, change management procedures, system documentation, and controls over financial reporting systems.
* Partner with IT, system administrators, and external vendors to resolve system issues and implement reporting solutions.

**Audit, Internal Controls, and Compliance**

* Maintain effective internal controls over financial reporting and support compliance with applicable SOX requirements.

* Partner with internal audit and external auditors on control testing, audit findings, and remediation activities.

* Lead and develop accounting and financial reporting personnel, fostering accountability, technical excellence, and continuous improvement.

title: Senior Financial Analyst, Clinical Finance
description:
Drug development shouldn’t be guesswork, not when patients are waiting.

Pathos is building a next-generation biotech with AI at the core. Not as a feature, but as the operating system for how medicines get developed. We believe most drugs don't fail because the science was wrong. They fail because they were tested in the wrong patients, with the wrong assumptions, in trials that couldn't answer the real question: who benefits, and why?

Pathos exists to change that. We're building the largest foundation model in oncology and pairing it with proprietary AI systems, deep oncology expertise, and 200+ petabytes of multimodal data linked to patient outcomes, so we can make development decisions with more precision, much earlier.

This is not theoretical. We’re well-capitalized and have the leadership to build a generational company. We invest in and advance our own clinical-stage programs, using our AI platform to sharpen trial design, patient selection and biomarker strategy. So therapies reach the patients most likely to benefit, sooner.

**How We Build**

Pathos does not operate like a traditional biotech. There is no middle management. There are no layers of approval. The company is designed, from the ground up, around small teams of 2–4 subject matter experts who each command hundreds of AI agents to do the work that used to require dozens of people.

Everyone builds. Everyone ships. Every function at Pathos — from clinical execution to asset selection to the foundation model itself — runs on this model. Our product velocity delivers meaningful outcomes in hours instead of weeks. This is not a future aspiration. It is how we operate today.

The people who thrive here are operators: deep experts who can specify what needs to happen, orchestrate AI agents to execute at scale, and make high-judgment calls that compound over time. If you have spent your career building and shipping AI systems at scale, this is the environment where that experience becomes a superpower.

**About the role**

We are seeking a Senior Financial Analyst, Clinical Finance to own the financial side of our clinical vendor base, from forecast and contract review through invoice review and monthly accruals.

This is a step up for an analyst with 2 to 4 years in biotech or pharma finance who wants to own a process end to end. You will report to our SVP of Finance and partner day to day with Clinical Operations, the accounting team, Legal on contract terms, and our CROs and vendors. The core of the job is knowing what is changing in each trial and making sure the budget, forecast and accruals keep pace. At Pathos, that work does not run on manual spreadsheets and inbox triage. You will use AI agents and automation to build repeatable processes that reduce errors, improve accuracy and surface insights we would otherwise miss.

### **What You Will Do**

#### **Clinical Spend Forecasting**

* Build and own the clinical trial forecast by vendor, study and cost category (CRO services, pass through costs, site grants, lab, technology, imaging, IRB).
* Hold a regular dialogue with Clinical Operations to capture changes as they happen: enrollment pace, site activation, protocol amendments, scope changes and timeline shifts.
* Translate each trial change into its cost and timing impact, and keep forecasts and estimates on the latest plan, not the one in the original contract.
* Produce the clinical inputs to the annual budget, quarterly reforecasts and cash runway models.

#### **Vendor Spend and Invoice Review**

* Maintain a tracker for every clinical vendor that matches each invoice line to its MSA, SOW, work order and executed change orders, and tracks remaining contract value by category.
* Support the clinical AP process: track incoming invoices in our AP platform, tie them to their POs and study, catch duplicates, and route them to Clinical Operations for review.
* Review vendor billing by hours, units, milestones and pass through costs against the contract and real study progress, and flag resource use that looks out of scope, overstaffed or ahead of the work before invoices are approved.
* Track CRO prefunded deposits and site grant funds: what has been prepaid, applied and credited back.
* Keep a running exceptions log and escalate each item for resolution with the vendor or a Pathos decision.

#### **Actuals Versus Forecast**

* Close the loop each month: compare invoiced and accrued spend to forecast by vendor and category, and explain the variances.
* Keep the clinical spend dashboard current and reconciled to Pathos billing and accounting platforms.
* Prepare monthly spend, burn and variance reporting for the SVP of Finance and Clinical Operations leadership.

#### **Clinical Procurement**

* Support the finance side of contracting: review SOW and change order budgets, compare pricing and rate cards to prior work, flag issues for the SVP of Finance, and confirm budget availability before signature.
* Provide vendor, study and budget details for purchase order setup in Bill.com.

#### **Clinical Accruals**

* Prepare the monthly clinical accrual for each vendor, built from vendor reported work, unit and milestone data, site activity and Clinical Operations input, for review by the SVP of Finance.
* Maintain accrual and prepaid schedules that support the accounting team’s journal entries and reclasses, and reconcile them to subsequent invoices.
* Support the annual audit and investor diligence with clear, documented clinical expense support.

### **Who You Are**

#### **Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics or a related field.
* 2 to 4 years as a financial analyst at a biotech, pharma company or CRO, with direct exposure to R&D or clinical trial costs across multiple studies.
* Working knowledge of how clinical trials are contracted and billed: MSAs, SOWs, change orders, pass through costs, site payments and prefunded deposits.
* Experience building forecasts and variance analyses.
* Understanding of accrual accounting and month end close. You can build an accrual from operational data with documented support.
* Advanced Excel: you build models others can follow, audit and update.
* A strong interest in using AI tools and automation in daily work, with examples of workflows you have streamlined or rebuilt to cut manual effort and errors.
* The confidence to question a vendor invoice and the judgment to work collaboratively with Clinical Operations.

#### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Hands on clinical accrual ownership for one or more studies.
* Experience with QuickBooks Online and Bill.com, or similar ERP and AP tools.
* Exposure to oncology trials.
* Experience on a small finance team where you covered several roles.
* CPA progress or MBA coursework.

#### **What Success Looks Like**

In your first year:

* Within 90 days, every active vendor has a current tracker reconciled to its contract, the GL and the spend dashboard.
* No overrun reaches an invoice unflagged, and trial changes show up in the forecast and accruals the same month.
* Clinical accruals close each month with documented support and no material true ups at audit.

### **Location**

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City office, with in-person attendance on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays.

The pay range for this role is:

100,000 - 120,000 USD per year (New York Office - ACLS East Tower)

title: Head of Finance Performance Management - Rail Infrastructure
description:
**Position Overview**

Siemens Mobility North America seeks an experienced finance leader to head Finance and Performance Management (FPM) for its Rail Infrastructure (RI) business. The role provides an independent, forward-looking view of performance, serves as a trusted sparring partner to RI and Finance leadership, and connects the business unit with North America and global stakeholders.

You will lead the RI FPM team and own the coordination, consolidation, analysis and communication of financial performance, combining strong governance with commercial insight, constructive challenge and pragmatic decision support in a complex project and product environment.

**What You Will Accomplish**

* Drive fact-based performance management, translating financial and operational data into a clear view of results, outlook, risks, opportunities and required actions.
* Act as an independent, solution-oriented partner who challenges assumptions and explains trade-offs without taking over operational ownership.
* Build a coherent RI financial narrative that links drivers, financial statements and management priorities across segments and stakeholders.
* Develop a high-performing, collaborative FPM team that balances business proximity with common North America standards and continuous capability building.
* Advance process harmonization, digitalization, analytics and responsible AI to improve finance quality, speed and productivity.

**Key Responsibilities**

Business Partnership and Performance Management

* Serve as principal FPM partner to RI leadership and the primary RI interface to North America regional and global finance.
* Monitor key financial and operational indicators to spot trends, deviations, risks and opportunities early and turn them into decision-relevant insights.
* Objectively challenge forecasts, budgets, business cases and assumptions; develop scenarios, sensitivities and fact-based recommendations.
* Deliver concise executive analyses explaining what changed, why it matters, what remains uncertain and where action is needed.

Planning, Forecasting, Reporting and Financial Integrity

* Lead the RI annual budget, monthly forecast and management reporting processes, from calendars and inputs through consolidation, review, commentary and submission.
* Ensure a complete, accurate and consistent view of P&L, balance sheet and cash flow, with transparent bridges between actuals, forecast, budget and prior outlook.
* Challenge the plausibility of business and project inputs, investigate unusual entries and variances, and make material risks, opportunities and adjustments visible in the outlook.
* Partner with Accounting, Commercial Project Management, Operations and others to align close impacts, assumptions and the financial storyline, while keeping accountability for source data and business decisions clear.
* Escalate material performance, cash, balance-sheet, compliance or control issues promptly, with the evidence decision makers need.

Governance, Process Excellence and Digitalization

* Reinforce finance governance, internal-control and reporting requirements; support audit readiness and documentation of significant assumptions and judgments.
* Clarify responsibilities and interfaces across FPM, the business, Accounting, CPM, Operations and central functions to avoid duplication, ownership gaps and “shadow” controlling structures.
* Drive common North America FPM standards and best practices, allowing fit-for-purpose differences for RI business models and segments.
* Sponsor simplification, automation, analytics and digital-finance initiatives, including SAC, SAP, standardized templates and responsible AI-enabled workflows.
* Regularly assess the value, effort and control implications of recurring reports and processes, prioritizing improvements in insight, reliability or productivity.

Leadership and Talent Development

* Lead, coach and develop a diverse finance team with clear priorities, quality standards, responsibilities and development goals.
* Foster trust, candid communication, accountability, collaboration and continuous learning across locations and organizational boundaries.
* Balance business support, governance and capacity, focusing resources on material topics and ensuring resilient coverage of critical recurring processes.
* Contribute to the North America FPM leadership team and the OneFPM agenda, including talent development, succession planning and cross-business collaboration.

Scope and Accountability

FPM owns financial transparency, process coordination, consolidation, independent challenge and management insight; business and functional owners remain accountable for operational plans, source assumptions, corrective actions and final decisions. The Head of FPM RI keeps these interfaces explicit, surfaces material issues and ensures temporary support does not become a permanent transfer of ownership.

**Required Knowledge, Skills and Experience**

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
* Typically 8+ years of progressive experience in controlling, FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial project management, or similar, including meaningful leadership responsibility.
* Proven ability to lead budgeting, forecasting, performance reporting and executive reviews in a complex matrix organization.
* Strong grasp of P&L, balance sheet and cash-flow interdependencies and how project, operational and commercial drivers shape financial outcomes.
* Excellent analytical judgment; able to distinguish facts, estimates and hypotheses, challenge assumptions and make uncertainty explicit.
* Executive-level communication skills, turning complex data into concise, decision-oriented messages for regional and international stakeholders.
* Proven people leader who coaches experienced professionals, sets direction and builds constructive relationships across functions and hierarchies.
* High integrity, resilience and sound judgment; able to prioritize and deliver reliable results under competing deadlines.
* Advanced proficiency with enterprise planning, reporting and analytics tools; experience with SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), SAP, data visualization, automation or AI-enabled finance workflows is an advantage.
* Experience in project-driven, infrastructure, transportation, or industrial businesses preferred.

title: Wealth Management, Portfolio Construction Strategy, Analyst
description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**  
  
  

Portfolio construction sits at the heart of how J.P. Morgan delivers advice to clients, and the Office of Portfolio Construction (OPC) is the firm's strategic engine behind it. We're seeking an energetic, intellectually curious Analyst to join the Portfolio Construction Strategy team — the front-office arm of OPC — to help shape how advisors across the U.S. Private Bank and U.S. Wealth Management build, review, and refine client portfolios.

OPC is a major initiative for the business, with a mission to elevate portfolio construction as a core differentiator of the Private Bank and Wealth Management and equip advisors to build portfolios aligned to each client's plan, grounded in our principles, and focused on after-tax outcomes. The group is focused on three pillars — establishing portfolio construction principles, tying strategy to portfolio action, and providing advisors with customized guidance they can scale — and operates across the Private Bank and U.S. Wealth Management, supporting 7,000+ advisors and more than $750B in investment assets. Our north star is embedding our advice and methodologies into the AI-powered tools (ConnectWealth and Portfolio Builder) that scale portfolio advice across every advisor.

You'll work alongside senior Strategists and partner closely with Global Investment Strategy, Investments Research, Managed Investments, Due Diligence, and regional Investments & Advice leaders — gaining a broad, cross-asset view of how portfolios actually get built through an after-tax lens at one of the world's leading wealth managers.

**Our Team**

The Portfolio Construction Strategy team is the advisor-facing engine of OPC. We own the firm's portfolio construction philosophy, drive the content and education that bring it to life, and partner with every region and channel across the Private Bank and U.S. Wealth Management to drive adoption. Working with a product-agnostic lens — across public and private assets, taxable and tax-exempt portfolios, and discretionary, advisory and brokerage accounts — we help advisors answer the questions that matter most for client portfolios: how to build a strategic asset allocation, how to deliver on client preferences such as high income or concentrated-equity diversification, how to size high-conviction ideas alongside a core portfolio, and how to drive tax-efficiency across the whole portfolio.

**Job Responsibilities**

As an Analyst on the Portfolio Construction Strategy team, you'll work under the guidance of senior Portfolio Construction and Tax-Aware Strategists and the US Head of Portfolio Construction Strategy. You'll start by supporting the team's core workstreams and, over time, aim to grow into a Portfolio Construction Strategist in your own right. In this role, you will:

* Support the development and rollout of our flagship Portfolio Construction content — including the Portfolio Construction Philosophy, Portfolio Construction Themes decks, Implementation Guide, sizing guidance primers, 1-pagers, and portfolio checklists — ensuring every piece is accurate, consistent, and on-message with our views.
* Partner on strategic initiatives such as the Expanded/Custom Strategic Asset Allocation framework, Portfolio Templates, and Framework for Taxes in Portfolio Construction — from design through advisor rollout.
* Help embed OPC methodologies into AI-powered advisor tools (ConnectWealth, Portfolio Builder, Co-Pilot, Connect Coach), working with Research, Risk, and technology partners to translate our frameworks into scalable product features.
* Work on large, complex client and prospect situations, helping advisors analyze portfolios and deliver solutions that win and retain assets.
* Prepare materials for broad advisor forums such as USPB Morning Meetings, U.S. Wealth Management National Calls, advisor training sessions, and senior leadership forums — including slides, talking points, and follow-up communications.
* Track progress against the team's deliverables across USPB and USWM; coordinate with stakeholders in Global Investment Strategy, Investments Research, Managed Investments, Due Diligence, Portfolio Analytics, and regional Investments & Advice leadership to keep workstreams on plan.
* Build a deep, foundational understanding of capital markets, asset allocation, tax-aware investing, and multi-asset portfolio construction.
* Successful analysts will build a clear development track into a full Portfolio Construction Strategist seat on the team, developing cross-asset expertise spanning public equities and fixed income, private markets, hedge funds, structured products, and more — given the breadth of the team's remit.

* 1–2 years of experience in wealth management, asset management, investment strategy, portfolio management, or another financial markets–related role.
* Genuine interest in financial markets, asset allocation, portfolio construction, and macro-level economics, with a strong willingness to learn and grow in these areas.
* Foundational understanding of taxes and how they influence portfolio decisions — including the impact on asset allocation and asset location — with an interest in deepening tax-aware investing expertise.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex portfolio and market concepts into clear, concise messages for advisors, senior leaders, and clients.
* Strong analytical and quantitative skills, with high proficiency in AI tools and comfort working with portfolio and performance data.
* Background in finance, economics, mathematics, statistics, or financial accounting;
* Exceptional organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities, workstreams, and stakeholders simultaneously with limited supervision.
* Strong business acumen and strategic thinking, with a demonstrated interest in driving organizational priorities and cross-functional initiatives.
* High standards of service and attention to detail — strong initiative, energy, intellectual curiosity, and the confidence to engage senior partners across the organization.
* Experience with portfolio analytics and data analysis tools (Excel, Python, or similar), and familiarity with portfolio construction and optimization concepts.
* Exposure to multi-asset investing — including private markets, alternatives, tax-aware investing, or structured solutions — and awareness of the key industry debates in portfolio construction today.
* Experience in business management, project management, or stakeholder engagement, particularly in a client- or advisor-facing financial services context.

**Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills**

title: Asset & Wealth Management, QIS, Quantitative Liquid Alternatives Portfolio Construction Analyst - New York
description:

Are you an intellectually curious, disciplined self-starter with a passion for financial markets and quantitative investing? The Quantitative Investment Strategies (QIS) team within Goldman Sachs Asset & Wealth Management is seeking an Analyst to join the Liquid Alternatives Portfolio Construction team. In this role, you will be on the front lines of active portfolio management - combining economic rationale, mathematical optimization, and advanced analytical tools to drive daily rebalancing, risk attribution, and portfolio performance across our liquid alternatives strategies.

**WHO WE ARE**

**Goldman Sachs Asset & Wealth Management** is one of the world's leading investment managers, providing institutional and individual investors with investment and advisory solutions across asset classes, industries and geographies. We help our clients navigate dynamic markets and identify the opportunities that shape their portfolios and long-term investment goals. We extend these global capabilities to the world's leading pension plans, sovereign wealth funds, central banks, insurance companies, financial institutions, endowments, foundations, individuals and family offices.

The **Quantitative Investment Strategies (QIS)** group is a market leader in quantitative portfolio management, using advanced quantitative methods to structure, manage, and monitor investment portfolios across quantitative equity, multi-asset, and alternative strategies. Within QIS, the **Liquid Alternatives** team delivers uncorrelated returns, factor-based strategies, and customized portfolio solutions to investors.

The ideal candidate is passionate about investing and motivated to deliver differentiated, uncorrelated returns. * Work with external parties, including elected officials, local and county governments, tenant associations, banks, affordable housing owners, management companies and limited partners to address distressed or underperforming buildings.

* Build OHP’s capacity to monitor its program operations and the performance of affordable housing in the agency’s portfolio.
* Lead the development and implementation of project plans supporting OHP initiatives that integrate processes and policies, improve operations, and strengthen customer service.

**Job Description**
-------------------

THE AGENCY
  
The Department of City Planning (DCP) plans for the future of New York City, working to create thriving and dynamic neighborhoods with access to housing and jobs, resilient infrastructure, and a vibrant public realm. The Department engages communities to develop inclusive plans, expands housing access and economic opportunity, and plans for long-term sustainability.
  
  
DCP supports the City Planning Commission in its annual review of hundreds of land use applications. The Department also advises on citywide strategic and capital planning, analyzes data, conducts policy analysis, and creates open data and civic engagement tools. DCP is also the custodian of the official City Map, which designates streets, parks and other public places.
  
  
Department of City Planning offers staff meaningful opportunities to help shape the future of New York City and address some of its most pressing challenges. The Department values public service, collaboration, and creativity, and supports professional development. Learn more about DCP and view current job openings at www.nyc.gov/planning.
  
  
THE DIVISION
  
DCP’s Fiscal Division strives to improve the agency’s financial responsibility and operational effectiveness by providing information, analysis, and administrative and technical support to programs and divisions throughout the agency. The Fiscal team’s daily operations include, but are not limited to, procurement, grant management, accounting for both payments and receivables, budgeting and financial reporting.
  
  
Within DCP’s Fiscal Division, the Procurement Unit oversees the acquisition of goods and services for programs and teams across the agency, ensuring compliance with all applicable rules, laws, and mandates, including but not limited to Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, State and Federal procurement policies, NYC Comptroller Directives, Mayor’s Directives, Department of Citywide Administrative Services’ guidelines, and the City Charter. The Procurement Unit also manages the agency’s existing portfolio of contracts and DCP’s Minority and Women-Owned Enterprise (M/WBE) program.  
  
  
  
THE JOB
  
The Procurement team is seeking to hire a detail-oriented, highly motivated Procurement Analyst. Reporting to the Agency Chief Contracting Officer, the Procurement Analyst will be responsible for processing goods and services requests associated with various procurement methods for divisional needs while adhering to the City's PPB Rules, State and Federal Procurement requirements as applicable, and other Citywide Directives.
  
  
Under the supervision of the Agency Chief Contracting Officer, the selected candidate will be expected to assist the Procurement Division with an array of procurement functions and related tasks including but not limited to:
  
  

* Analyzing incoming procurement requests to determine appropriate procurement methods and reviewing request details for accuracy and adequacy.
* Supporting agency business units to meet purchasing needs efficiently and expeditiously, ensuring purchases are made in adherence with internal and external procurement policies and procedures.
* Working closely with Fiscal and business units to address funding needs for purchases and gathering technical requirements, respectively.
* Utilizing FMS, PASSPort and OCP Portals to process purchases under New York State Requirement Contracts, New York City Requirement Contracts, Punch-Out (DO1) Catalogs, and/or Micro-purchase orders.
* Processing encumbrance increases and decreases as needed to facilitate payment processing and PO closeouts.
* Corresponding with vendors, obtaining quotes, responding to vendor inquiries, and troubleshooting order issues that may arise.
* Processing p-card purchases in compliance with Citywide P-Card Purchasing Policies and Requirements and performing monthly p-card reconciliations and reporting tasks.
* Supporting larger contract processes, such as preparing bid and/or solicitation specifications, facilitating contract registration, etc.
* Performing data entry, maintaining agency procurement trackers and records, and preparing various reports, etc.
* Performing other ad-hoc tasks as assigned.

  
PREFERRED SKILLS:
  
  

* Knowledge of all Procurement Policy Board Rules.
* Knowledge of City systems including FMS, PASSPort, The City Record Online, Checkbook, etc.
* Experience managing procurements from start to completion.
* Ability to adapt to a fluid work environment and changing needs and priorities.
* Strong analytical and negotiation skills.
* Strong organizational skills.
* Effective, clear and persuasive oral and written communications.

description:
**Who We Are**
==============

At Justworks, you'll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, great benefits, wellness program offerings, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the startup community. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people.
